title: Chapter 84
content:
Wheeled through the double doors of the trauma bay on a gurney, Wang Ryun looked like a corpse.

Exsanguinated down to a pale, paper-thin white, his frame was entirely motionless. The attending surgeon had made it clear: had Wang Han not clamped the severed artery and administered field trauma dressing on that rooftop, Ryun would have bled out before ever reaching an ambulance.

How the hell did they know?

The operational timeline was an absolute black box—known exclusively to the three of them and Kang Il-hyun. To keep their footprint invisible, they hadn't even utilized Il-hyun's security detail for transit. Yet an armed tactical kill-team had been staged inside the apartment, lying in wait. No matter how many times Jakyeong turned it over in his head, the pieces refused to fit.

Surgical staff rushed past, carrying unit after unit of packed red blood cells into the theater. Standing rooted to the linoleum, Jakyeong caught a brief glimpse of Ryun’s limp, blood-drained arm through the glass before turning away, unable to stomach the sight.

In the waiting area, Wang Han sat slumped on a plastic chair, his eyes glazed and hollow. Jakyeong sank into the seat beside him, staring at the illuminated Operating sign. Every time the double doors swung open, his heart plummeted into his stomach.

Han reached over, his heavy, calloused hand resting gently against Jakyeong’s hair.

"He'll pull through, Wei. That bastard is far too stubborn to die."

Jakyeong ground his teeth. Whenever panic had seized him as a child in Macau, Han had always rested a hand on his head, offering that same quiet reassurance. And miraculously, things had always turned out fine. He desperately prayed the old magic still held.

Yet beneath the worry, a suffocating guilt gnawed at his ribs. If he hadn't left his night-vision gear on the roof, Ryun wouldn't have leaned over the parapet. Even if ambushed, a disciplined operative like Ryun wouldn't have been blindsided so cleanly.

Sensing the boy's internal spiral, Han gently patted his back, offering silent comfort.

Time dragged by with agonizing slowness. One hour. Two hours.

Han stepped outside to make a call. Left alone under the harsh fluorescent lights, Jakyeong paced the corridor before pulling out his phone. He hovered over Kang Il-hyun’s contact, thumb hesitating over the screen. He's likely asleep. But an operational compromise of this scale demands an immediate report.

Han returned from the lobby, shaking his head. He had tried reaching Ryun’s girlfriend to deliver the news, but her line was completely dead. Which made zero sense—Ryun had literally been speaking to her minutes before the breach.

Just as the silence grew unbearable, the surgical doors finally hissed open.

Ryun was wheeled out on a mobile ICU bed, his face as white as the hospital linen, flanked by a dense forest of IV lines and transfusion bags swaying overhead.

Han lunged forward, grabbing the surgeon's arm. "Doctor... how is he?"

The surgeon pulled down his surgical mask, letting out a weary breath. "He suffered massive hemorrhage, but his vitals have stabilized. The critical vascular damage was contained thanks to immediate, exceptional field compression. As long as we manage postoperative infection, he will survive."

"Thank you, Doctor. Thank you so much."

Han bowed repeatedly, his posture so low he looked ready to prostrate on the floor. Jakyeong bowed in kind, exchanging a look with Han as a heavy, synchronized sigh of relief washed over both of them.

"Worried over nothing," Jakyeong muttered with a faint, tired smirk.

"Who was worried about him?" Han countered, letting the tension bleed out into dry humor. "I was worried about our supply chain. If that idiot died, who was going to procure our black-market munitions?"

"Right. Who else would buy us defective gear?"

Trading quiet, ridiculous jabs, they followed the orderly toward the recovery ward. As they reached the elevators, the phone in Jakyeong's pocket buzzed.

An incoming text from an unlisted number.

He tapped the screen—and froze mid-stride.

It was a surveillance photograph: Park Tae-soo sitting across a café table from Ryun’s girlfriend, Yoon Mi-ra.

"..."

Jakyeong swiped to the next image.

Tae-soo was handing a heavy, black duffel bag across the table to the woman.

The blood drained from Jakyeong's face. What is this? Why is Kang Il-hyun's right hand meeting Ryun's girlfriend in secret?

Noticing the halt, Han looked back over his shoulder. "What's wrong, Wei?"

Jakyeong shoved the handset deep into his pocket, closing the distance in two quick strides. "Do you have Ryun-ge’s operational burner on you?"

Han reached into his jacket, passing over the battered device.

To maintain strict operational security, the team always carried dual handsets: modern smartphones for civilian use, and stripped-down, analog burner phones for mission coordination and target routing. The encrypted channels and operational schedules were shared exclusively on the burners.

Yet Ryun had constantly broken protocol, using his mission burner to trade sweet nothings with his lover—earning him endless, furious scoldings from Han.

Jakyeong punched in the PIN and dialed Yoon Mi-ra’s private line.

Just as Han had reported, the automated carrier message played immediately: The number you have dialed is currently powered off.

Jakyeong’s gaze sharpened into ice. He redialed twice more. Same dead tone.

Scrolling through their recent SMS logs, the messages were entirely benign—routine exchanges of domestic affection.

Without a word, Jakyeong popped the plastic casing off the burner, ripped the lithium battery from its housing, and slammed the handset violently against the concrete corridor wall.

Crack.

The chassis fractured open. Jakyeong tore the internal motherboard from the frame, inspecting the micro-circuitry under the fluorescent lights.

His eyes narrowed into razor slits.

Han leaned in close. Nestled right beside the primary cellular antenna was a microscopic transmitter chip smaller than a thumbnail.

An active hardware tap.

Han let out a stunned, devastated gasp. How long had it been planted? Every word, every coordination briefing, every target route discussed in Ryun’s presence had been broadcast live to an outside listener.

Staring at the silicone bug with pure, murderous venom, Jakyeong popped the chip into his mouth.

He clamped his molars down, grinding the hardware into pulverized dust until the sharp edges tore his gums, drawing blood. He spat the crushed metal into a nearby biohazard bin with a wet ptoo.

Wiping the smear of crimson from his lips, neither man could bring himself to walk into Ryun’s room. They simply collapsed back onto the plastic waiting chairs in dead, suffocating silence.

Standing on the private balcony of his presidential suite in Jeju, Kang Il-hyun dragged hard on a fresh cigarette.

Down in the plaza below, an angry mob of protestors was chanting through megaphones, brandishing painted banners against the resort construction. Though claiming to be a civic environmental coalition, their builds, scars, and aggressive posture screamed bottom-tier street muscle hired on short notice.

Fabricating an eleventh-hour environmental protest was an obvious corporate sabotage play. And of all times, they had pulled this stunt right when Lee Ja-kyeong was finally showing a sliver of sweet, jealous affection.

Having been forced onto a red-eye flight before he could even properly taste the kid's mouth, Il-hyun was in a foul, homicidal mood.

Grinding the cigarette filter between his teeth, a cruel smirk pulled at the corner of his lips.

"Fucking roaches... I should douse the entire plaza in jet fuel and fry them alive."

The clash had already escalated into an all-out brawl at dawn, landing their corporate legal team at the local precinct. According to the site director, the protest ringleader had specifically hurled vile insults regarding Il-hyun’s late parents, deliberately provoking the construction foremen into throwing the first punch. A calculated trap, executed flawlessly.

Il-hyun jammed his hands into his trouser pockets, exhaling gray smoke into the humid sea air. Irritating vermin everywhere I look.

The balcony doors slid back, and Park Tae-soo stepped out.

"President Kang. You need to take this call."

Tae-soo’s voice maintained its usual flat cadence, yet the tempo was a fraction of a second faster than normal. Recognizing the subtle shift, Il-hyun snatched the satellite handset and pressed it to his ear.

It was the tactical lead assigned to the Seoul protection detail—the unit tasked with shadowing Lee Ja-kyeong in his absence.

Listening to the report, the relaxed arrogance vanished from Il-hyun’s face, hardening into an expression of arctic, terrifying malice.

"Which hospital?"

The operative rattled off the medical center in Gangnam. Il-hyun barked an immediate order to transfer the patient to Haewon’s private VIP trauma facility under heavy armed escort, then terminated the call.

Below, the megaphones continued their deafening chants.

Il-hyun’s gaze remained locked on the pavement as he addressed his security chief.

"Prep the chopper. We're flying back to Seoul."

"Yes, sir."

Il-hyun crushed the cigarette out against the stone railing, his jaw ticking violently.

He didn't need to investigate to know whose hand had orchestrated this ambush. But how the operational coordinates had leaked remained a mystery. He had dialed Jakyeong’s secure line multiple times, but the boy wasn't answering.

Though the field report stated the injury was merely a superficial graze along the arm, the thought of his little stray caught in a crossfire made his blood boil.

My poor cat must be terrified out of his mind.

I need to get back and soothe him.

Jakyeong stepped out of the hospital's outdoor smoking shelter, tossing his spent filter into the receptacle.

The torrential rain of the early morning had burned away, replaced by a blistering, midsummer sun beating mercilessly against the pavement. Wearing the same damp, blood-spattered tactical clothes from the night before left him feeling filthy and raw.

He had redialed Yoon Mi-ra’s number dozens of times, but by mid-morning, the carrier automated response had transitioned to: This number is no longer in service.

Their worst-case scenario had materialized with brutal clarity. Han and Jakyeong were shattered—paralyzed by the question of how on earth they were going to break the truth to Ryun when he finally woke from the anesthesia. Ryun had regained consciousness briefly an hour ago, but the heavy painkillers had pulled him straight back under.

Letting out a heavy, weary sigh, Jakyeong walked toward the main entrance when a sleek black foreign sedan glided up the driveway, blocking his path.

As Jakyeong moved to sidestep the vehicle, the passenger door swung open, and a tall man in a dark tailored suit stepped out, barring his way.

"Mr. Lee Ja-kyeong?"

Jakyeong lifted his chin, his dark eyes locking onto the man's face. The features were instantly familiar—Chairman Kang’s senior executive secretary.

As Jakyeong stepped back, his hand instinctively drifting toward his waistband, the heavy, tinted rear glass of the sedan glided down smoothly.

Jakyeong’s posture stiffened into stone.

Chairman Kang.

A full year had passed since their last encounter, yet the old patriarch still radiated the unyielding, lethal aura of an aging apex predator.

"Get in," the Chairman said, his voice flat as a tombstone. "We have matters to discuss."

Jakyeong met the old man's stare with cold, unblinking hostility.

"Shouldn't you be heading to Kim Dong-myung’s funeral parlor instead of loitering outside a hospital, Chairman?"

"I have no idea what you are referring to."

"Keep playing the ignorant elder. It’s always been your greatest theatrical specialty."

"You truly believe I ordered last night's strike?"

Jakyeong let out a sharp, derisive scoff. "Who else? Are you going to claim Kang Il-hyun orchestrated a hit on his own contracted asset?"

The Chairman offered no verbal defense, prompting Jakyeong to sneer in contempt. Dropping a few staged surveillance photographs to frame Il-hyun was an amateur play. While Jakyeong was far from trusting Kang Il-hyun with his life, he knew the man wasn't stupid enough to sabotage his own operational board. There was zero tactical gain in doing so.

Which left Chairman Kang as the sole architect behind the ambush.

If I had my piece on me, I’d put two hollow-points through this old bastard's skull right now.

Jakyeong bared his teeth in a razor-sharp, crooked smirk.

"Watch your back, old man. I always collect on blood debts with compound interest."

"Such insolent tongue from a hired gun."

"I'm off your payroll, Chairman. Professional courtesy is dead."

Jakyeong turned to walk away, but the Chairman’s voice cut through the air once more:

"I hear you and President Kang share... quite an intimate arrangement these days."

Jakyeong’s brow pinched. Why beat around the bush? Just ask if we're fucking.

"Do you know what became of the previous companions who shared President Kang’s bed?"

Jakyeong stopped, looking back over his shoulder with dry disdain. "Am I supposed to take an interest in Kang Il-hyun's dating history?"

The Chairman smiled, looking thoroughly amused. "Aren't you even mildly curious? About their fates?"

"..."

"Whether they are currently walking among the living... or rotting six feet under the dirt?"

The nuance was dark, deliberate, and poisonous. Jakyeong offered no reply, watching the Chairman’s features settle into a chilling, grandfatherly mask.

"It is a pity you belong to his faction. You would have made a splendid hound in my kennel."

"Keep dreaming."

"Indeed. But heed a word of wisdom from an old man: do not place your faith in him. When the true crisis arrives... Kang Il-hyun will be the very first to cut your leash and throw you to the wolves."

Before Jakyeong could tell the patriarch to choke on his warning, the tinted glass glided upward, and the black sedan smoothly pulled away into traffic.

Jakyeong stood on the curb, glaring after the retreating exhaust with his fists clenched tight.

Watching the ruthless dynamic play out, he found himself almost feeling a perverse shred of pity for Kang Il-hyun. To have a biological father who treated his only surviving heir like a rabid dog marked for the slaughterhouse...

Fuck. No wonder the bastard turned into a complete psychopath.
